jobs.description: We are looking for an Electrical Commissioning Specialist at Academic Work Finland Oy in Helsinki, Vantaa, Kerava, and surrounding areas. This role involves commissioning electrical systems within L0-L6 levels, collaborating with multidisciplinary teams, and ensuring the safe and controlled commissioning of data centers. The ideal candidate has a degree in Electrical Engineering or a related field and extensive experience in testing, commissioning, or maintenance of complex electrical systems. They must be fluent in English, have expertise in critical power distribution and protection principles, and be able to evaluate technical documentation and resolve issues independently.
what_we_expect: Degree in Electrical Engineering or a related technical field, several years of hands-on experience in testing, commissioning, or maintaining complex electrical systems.

Experience in data centers or other mission-critical environments, such as power plants, hospitals, or industrial facilities, and a proven track record in managing test programs, cross-disciplinary interfaces, and technical problem-solving under pressure.
Deep expertise in critical power distribution, protection principles, and the complete L0–L6 commissioning lifecycle, including BAS/EPMS interfaces and integrated system testing logic.
Analytical, highly organized, fluent in English, strong ability to evaluate technical documentation, perform root-cause analysis on test deviations, and independently drive issue resolution.
Willingness to work on-site around Finland, handle non-standard working hours when needed, and start on short notice in an international project environment.
job_responsibilities: Reviewing and developing commissioning plans, responsibility matrixes, test programs, test scripts and acceptance criteria.
Assessing the commissioning readiness of equipment and systems prior to the start of testing phases.
Participating in Factory Acceptance Tests (FAT), evaluating results, and documenting findings.
Providing technical support for L2-level equipment and installation inspections, as well as L3-level start-up and functional tests.
Planning, monitoring, verifying results for L4-level system and functional tests.
Supporting the planning and execution of the L5 Integrated System Test (IST) phase and verifying inter-system functionality.
what_we_offer: A key role in the safe and controlled commissioning of a technically demanding data center.
An opportunity to work with critical electrical systems and integrated testing in an international environment.
A vantage point at the interface of the client, commissioning organization, designers, contractors, and equipment suppliers.
Support from Granlund's extensive expertise in data centers, electrical systems, automation, and project management.
Continuous recruitment process with two tests: one personality test and one cognitive test to find the right talent for the right position.

Respond to the different needs of customers with a solid experience in the sale of construction products.

Valid driver's license and a car in use.

jobs.meta_description: Looking for a Doctoral researcher in computational weld mechanics job in Lappeenranta? LUT University is seeking motivated candidates—apply today.
jobs.description: LUT University invites applications for a doctoral researcher position in computational weld mechanics. This role involves developing advanced simulation methods for welded high-strength steel structures, focusing on the analysis of local heat-affected zone behavior and predicting local property variations. The successful candidate will contribute to the development of next-generation simulation methods, collaborate with international research teams, and benefit from professional development opportunities. The position offers competitive salary and flexible working hours, with a starting salary of approximately EUR 3,100 per month. Interested candidates should submit their applications by October 15, 2026, and provide a cover letter, CV, degree certificates, and references.
what_we_expect: A master's degree (M.Sc. Or equivalent) in a relevant field such as mechanical engineering, materials engineering, welding engineering, computational mechanics, or another relevant discipline.
A solid background in numerical modelling, materials science, solid mechanics, finite element methods, programming, and/or welding technology.
Ability to work independently, communicate findings clearly, and collaborate effectively within the international research community.
Proficiency in English, both written and spoken, for performing the duties of the role.
Willingness to travel for project-related travel within Finland, participation in international conferences, and opportunities for research mobility with partner universities in Europe.
job_responsibilities: Conduct research on the analysis of local heat-affected zone (HAZ) behaviour in welded high-strength steels through computational weld mechanics (CWM) and phase-transformation modelling.
Collaborate with national and international partner universities, such as University of Oulu (Finland), KTH Royal Institute of Technology (Sweden), and Chemnitz University of Technology (Germany).
Contact details of two references (if available).
what_we_offer: Develop your scientific expertise and research skills.
Salary determined according to the Finnish university salary system (requirement level 2), starting salary approximately EUR 3,100 per month, depending on experience and qualifications.
Work starts in December 2026, with a one-year term (including a six-month trial period) and may be extended for up to three additional years, depending on the progress of your studies and research.

Work is based at the Lappeenranta campus, with flexible working hours supporting work-life balance, total of 1,612 annual working hours in accordance with the collective agreement for Finnish universities.

About Bittium.
